svg.text: Common-date intersection vs. masked union panel (concrete example: 6 tickers x 12 dates)
A panel = rows (trading dates) x columns (tickers). Each date is a cross-sectional graph snapshot for the GAT; tickers have different listing dates, so early dates have missing cells.
Listing dates: A,B,C from t1 · D from t4 · E from t6 · F from t8 (first listed day = lookback warmup, not yet a valid node).
keep only dates where EVERY ticker has data
(faded ✓ = data existed but the whole date is dropped)
keep ALL dates; per-date masks pick valid nodes
Only t8-t12 survive = 5 usable dates; t1-t7 discarded for ALL tickers.
F's late listing (t8) alone removes 7 dates from every ticker.
-> low statistical power, early history lost,
All 12 dates usable = more train/test dates -> higher power.
Late-listed tickers included on the dates they exist
Each date keeps only its valid (green) nodes for loss + attention.
The graph snapshot adapts its node set per date via node_mask
E, F not yet listed -> masked out (still present for A-D)
F listed at t8 -> now a valid node; graph grows to 6
